info.title: Afridict Backend API
info.description: Draft contract foundation for Afridict. No endpoints are implemented or declared yet. HTTP operations will be added as their domain semantics and authorization requirements are reviewed. This artifact is not a production API release. Financial values use exact integer strings with explicit units; pending execution must remain distinguishable from finalized settlement.

UnsignedIntegerString.description: Exact non-negative integer serialized as a decimal string. Never parse financial values through JavaScript Number. Every containing field must define its asset or unit, scale, maximum value and rounding rule before use in an operation.

RequestId.description: Opaque server-issued request correlation identifier. Contains no personal information or credentials. It is not an idempotency key.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Each operation must document its possible codes and recovery behavior. Clients must handle unknown codes safely.

message.description: Safe human-readable explanation. Clients must not branch on this text. Must not expose stack traces, raw provider payloads, identity evidence or secrets.
examples: The request does not satisfy the operation's validation rules.

ApiError.description: Shared draft error body. Resource-specific validation details, HTTP status mappings and retry behavior must be defined per operation. A transport failure does not establish that a financial command failed.

RequestId.description: Server-issued request correlation identifier, returned as X-Request-Id. Echoed as request_id in error bodies.

x-operation-review-requirements: Stable operationId, purpose, authorization scopes and resource-level access rules
Validated request and response schemas with synthetic success and error examples
Exact financial units, scale, domain bounds and rounding rules
Explicit pending and terminal states with polling or event recovery guidance
Idempotency scope, equivalence, retention, concurrency and conflict behavior for commands
Pagination, filtering, ordering and quotas where applicable
HTTP status mappings, stable error codes, request IDs and safe retry guidance
Mock fixtures, generated client types and server conformance verification
